annotations.text:
Two destinations

Money and Plan. That is the whole navigation.

Today, Spending and Cards were one question at three zoom levels, and splitting them made you carry the same period in your head across three screens. Plan is the only view that asks something else — it produces a decision, not a picture.

What folded where

Today + Spending + Cards → Money, as four sections down one page: the glance, what you owe, where it went, every transaction.

Cards stop being a page. The four cards with nothing urgent collapse to one quiet table, and a card's statements, limit history and reported rewards move into a drawer.

Evaluate → Plan. Statements + Review → Data.

One scope, one screen

Collapsing the tabs makes the period control unambiguous: there is one, at the top, and everything below it obeys — except balances and limits, which say so, because a balance has no period.

The transaction browser keeps its own filters, since filtering is not the same act as scoping.

Data is a utility, not a tab

It sits right-aligned with a count, because a chore should be surfaced by number rather than by permanent real estate.

CORRECTION: an earlier version of this note claimed 24 uncategorised rows carried AED 464,285. That was wrong. Those rows sit on two bank accounts and a credit facility, all flagged include_in_spending = 0, so the engine correctly excludes them from spend. Real uncategorised card spend is zero and the queue is empty. Ranking the queue by value is still right -- the API already does it, weighted by money not row count -- just not for the reason given here.

Colour was computed, not judged

The shipped palette declares six categorical hues but carries five: --s3 and --s6 are both greens, 1.6 deltaE apart under deuteranopia, and --s6 has no dark step at all.

Every candidate sixth hue tested collided with an existing slot. Blue / orange / green passes all-pairs in both modes, so the categorical set is three — used only on Plan, where the cards genuinely are the subject.
